# Scaling a two-limb number by a power of two

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/Statements.v, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `mul_pow2_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $z$ of $x c$:

$$z \approx x c.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x = x_0 + x_1$, $z = z_0 + z_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ldexp(x, n)` | `Expansion<T, 2>`, `int` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | $c = 2^n$, for an `n` with $2^n$ a number of `T`; otherwise $c$ is NaN and nothing is claimed |
| `half(x)` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | $c = 1/2$ |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.
- $c$ is a power of two: $c = 2^n$ for an integer $n$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $z$ is normalized: $z_0 = \mathrm{RN}(z_0 + z_1)$.
- $\lvert z - x c\rvert \le \eta$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`; `kairn::traits` exports them rounded up to `T`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $2^{-1074} \approx 4.9407 \times 10^{-324}$ | $2^{-149} \approx 1.4013 \times 10^{-45}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0.0`, `0x1p-1074` | `0.0f`, `0x1p-149f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0.0`, `0x1p-1074` | `0.0f`, `0x1p-149f` |

The compiled constants are the entry `ldexp` of `kairn::traits<Expansion<T, 2>>`: `unit` and `tiny` bound the error relative to the exact result, `unit_computed` and `tiny_computed` relative to the computed one ($\lvert \text{error}\rvert \le \mathtt{unit\_computed}\,\lvert\text{computed}\rvert + \mathtt{tiny\_computed}$).

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits and any exponent range, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `mul_pow2_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/MulPow2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/MulPow2.v), against `mul_pow2_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition mul_pow2_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall x0 x1 c : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  fmt emin prec c ->
  (exists n : Z, c = bpow radix2 n) ->
  let '(z0, z1) := mul_pow2_2 emin prec tie_even x0 x1 c in
  normalized_2 emin prec z0 z1 /\
  Rabs ((z0 + z1) - ((x0 + x1) * c)) <= 1 * eta emin.
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** both limbs scaled, then Fast2Sum (Milestone 1 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/mul_pow2_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/mul_pow2_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`, rounded to nearest; `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`fast_two_sum`](fast_two_sum.md).

```
# A 2-limb number times a power of two c: exact unless a product is rounded in the subnormal
# range. It ends with Fast2Sum because the second product, rounded there, can land half a gap from
# the first, and the pair is then no longer normalized. Its exactness when each product is zero or
# at least 2^(p-1) eta in magnitude is not stated: the vocabulary has no such condition yet.

h        = prod(x0, c)
l        = prod(x1, c)
(z0, z1) = fast_two_sum(h, l)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#mul_pow2_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest error / bound | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 61 402 136 | 0 | 0.749144 | no |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 40 runners on 3 machines | 61 583 944 | 0 | 0.750000 | no |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 5 258 044 | 0 | 0.746094 (`fp:6:-12:4`) | no |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only `from_limbs_unchecked` or writing `limb[]` directly can make.
